- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect bearish sentiment’s fading.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days); cap forecast peaks at 1.5–2x recent high.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3-5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct; add slight upward bias to counteract.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model tends to lag true price movements by 1–2 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is trending.
- If sentiment history shows repeated volatility (e.g., alternating +/–0.3), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecasts with weighted average of 3–5 prior days.
- When sentiment is neutral or flat (±0.1), model often overreacts; dampen forecast volatility by 10–20% unless strong trend persists.
